title: Nautical Miles Between Coordinates
description: Compute the great-circle distance in nautical miles between two coordinates with Nautical Miles Between Coordinates — sea miles, exact. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, JFK to London Heathrow is 2,991.4 nautical miles — at a freighter's 15 knots that is 199 hours at sea, about 8.3 days, before weather gets its vote.
quick_answer: Nautical Miles Between Coordinates measures the great-circle distance between two coordinate points and reports it in nautical miles — the sea and air unit, defined as exactly 1.852 kilometres. Enter the pair and read the sea distance: the number passage plans, ETAs and fuel calculations are built from.

examples.label: Example · The Atlantic in sea miles

body.t: JFK–Heathrow: 5,540.0 km = 2,991.4 nm. A jet at ~500 mph covers the same ground in about 6.9 hours of flying — the unit stays nautical in the cockpit because charts, and the latitude scale itself, are built on it.

examples.label: Example · Why the unit fits the sea

body.t: One nautical mile is one arcminute of latitude — sail 60 nm north and your latitude gains exactly one degree. No land unit marries the chart like that, which is why this conversion is a translation between civilisations, not just numbers.

popular_table.intro: The unit against the land world's measures.
popular_table.note: The international nautical mile is exactly 1,852 metres by definition (1929, adopted universally since). Historical sea miles varied by nation — modern charts and this calculator use the exact figure.

faq: Great-circle (haversine) between the coordinates on a spherical Earth, converted at exactly 1.852 km per nautical mile — the method the tool's own note states, at full precision.
Why not road or shipping-lane distance?
This is the geometric sea distance between the points. Real passages follow lanes, coasts and weather, and run longer — the plan adds those; the baseline must be the true minimum first.
Hours = nautical miles ÷ knots, by the unit's definition. 165.3 nm (New York–Boston) at 20 knots is about 8.3 hours of steaming, harbour time excluded.
Decimal degrees paste directly; DMS and other dresses convert first with the Coordinate Converter, so the pair enters cleanly.
Spherical geometry costs well under a percent against the ellipsoid — irrelevant beside weather routing. Bad coordinates, as ever, are the true error source.
Yes, alongside kilometres — but the nautical figure leads, because at sea the other two are the translations, not the original.
Historical units varied (the old British sea mile ran 6,080 feet). Modern work uses exactly 1,852 m; antique distances deserve antique suspicion and a conversion note.
